newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH BANK CSOB 1996 AUDITED PROFIT RISES- AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH BANK CSOB 1996 AUDITED PROFIT RISES- AGENCY.

text.p: Czech state-controlled bank Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB) posted a 3.0 billion crown audited 1996 net profit, according to international accounting standards, after 2.85 billion in 1995, CTK news agency said on Tuesday.
It said CSOB's end-year balance sheet total rose to 206.7 billion crowns from 190.2 billion.
The agency quoted CSOB General Director Pavel Kavanek as saying that decreasing provision requirements helped to increase the profit despite falling interest margins.

CTK said CSOB would propose to put the entire profit into general reserves in order to boost the bank's capital adequacy ratio to "over 12 percent" from 1995's 9.96 percent and not pay out any dividend.
CSOB officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Czech National Bank and government institutions hold a 67 percent stake in CSOB. The National Bank of Slovakia also holds a 24 percent stake. The remaining shares are held by trading companies of the two countries.
